newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab Auto sees probable Q4 1998 profit.
newsitem.headline: Saab Auto sees probable Q4 1998 profit.

text.p: Robert Hendry, Managing Director of Swedish luxury carmaker Saab Automobile AB, said on Monday he expected the company to turn a profit in the fourth quarter of 1998, the Swedish news agency TT reported.
Hendry said, however, that he did not expect Saab to return a full-year profit before 1999. Saab is half-owned by General Motors and half by Swedish investment company Investor.
Hendry was talking at the launch of the new 9-5 top-end model, said on Friday it expected to sell 10,000 of the new cars in 1997.
Analysts say the company's future could ride on the success of this model. With only two platforms and plagued by financial woes for most of the 1990s, Saab Auto can ill afford a flop.

In 1996 Saab Automobile swung into the red, posting a pre-tax loss of 1.24 billion crowns -- of which about half was because of marketing costs -- compared to a profit of 148 million crowns it posted a year earlier.
"We have invested 5.5 billion crowns in development work," on the new model, Hendry said, adding costs had been restrained because of Saab's cooperation with GM.
